title: In a 21-site field test, 38 percent of heat pump installs needed a new electrical panel

sentences.text: Across 21 heat pump installs, 38 percent needed a new electrical panel. Was it in your quote?

assertions.text: Across 21 sites installing cold-climate heat pump prototypes, 38% needed a new panel.
qualifications: s02 says in the narration what the 38 percent is measured on: 21 sites in a field test of cold-climate prototypes, read from the installers' invoices, not a national survey, so the share is not the odds for the viewer's house.

sentences.note: Revision 2 answers the reviewer's warning on revision 1: "The quote covers the heat pump" asserted something about what a contractor's quote includes, which no passage bears on. The clause is now the Short's question, which is what the reviewer's suggestion asked for, and the opening is the figure itself, as the eyebrow ONE FIGURE FROM THE RECORD wants. The title keeps the population (21-site field test) the hook no longer names, and s02 names it in the narration.

sentences.text: Those were cold-climate prototypes in a field test, not a national survey, so that share is not the odds for your house.

assertions.text: The 38% share comes from a field test at 21 sites installing cold-climate heat pump prototypes, gathered from the invoices of the HVAC contractors used at all 21 sites, not from a national survey of homes.
qualifications: s02 is itself the qualification the record carries on s01: twenty-one homes taking cold-climate prototypes in a field test, measured from the installers' invoices, and not a national sample from which an ordinary home's odds could be read.

sentences.note: Carries the Short's first qualification inside the finding: the population behind the 38 percent. The figures stay in the assertion so the narration does not read 21 and 38 again. Word for word as revision 1: the reviewer approved it and dispositioned its one warning, and asked that it be kept intact through any revision of s03 and s04.

sentences.text: Where electrical upgrades were needed, they alone ran $3,750 to $8,970 in labour and materials, before the heat pump itself.

assertions.text: In that field test, the total costs for electrical upgrades varied between $3,750 and $8,970, for labor and materials only, not including the heat pump prototype.
qualifications: s03 places the limitation beside its own figure: the range is labour and materials for the electrical work only, at the sites where that work was needed, and it sits before the heat pump itself.

sentences.note: Revision 2 takes the reviewer's wording. Revision 1 said "Where the panel had to change", which attached the range to panel replacements; the passage attaches it to each site's electrical upgrades as a whole, and Table 11 shows most of that work was breakers for auxiliary heat, wiring and service lines rather than a new panel. The sentence now names what the figure measures, which is what the assertion always said.

sentences.text: For a 200-amp panel on its own, a retrofit cost report cites an outside estimate of $1,954, plus wiring for each new circuit.

assertions.text: A retrofit cost report cites an outside estimate for the typical cost of a 200 amp electrical panel upgrade, $1,954 (Lane, 2019), in addition to the electrical costs for each dedicated circuit run to new electrical appliances.
qualifications: s04 keeps the $1,954 beside what it measures, a 200-amp panel on its own plus the wiring for each new circuit, and s03 keeps its own range beside what that measures, a site's electrical upgrades entire. The Short draws no comparison between them.

sentences.note: Revision 2 answers both blocking findings on revision 1 and departs from the package's third carries entry, which the reviewer ruled the passage does not support. "A larger retrofit database" is gone: the report attributes the $1,954 to Lane (2019) and recorded only two panel upgrades of its own, so the narration says it cites an outside estimate. "Well under that range" is gone too, with no replacement comparison: the $1,954 is one item and s03's range is a whole site's electrical work, so each sentence now names its own measure and the Short never ranks them or calls the field test's range the high end.

sentences.text: What the whole install really costs is the question the full inquiry takes on.
